jo: quick heads-up — onboarding orion-9b:int4 on canary showing sporadic OOMs under bursty mixed-chat traffic. appears to correlate with big default max_new_tokens and short batch windows.

nina: can you paste the minimal logs / alloc trace?

jo: clipped logs: 
```
2026-04-05T07:22:11Z runtime: gpu0 alloc failed allocating 1.05GiB
runtime: slab#21 used=3.0GB free=7MB frag_index=0.41
request: model=orion-9b int4 seq=1024 max_new_tokens=400 batch_window_ms=5
stack: kv_cache::alloc -> slot_compactor -> kernel_alloc -> oom
```

raj: frag_index ~0.4 — yeah that's high. immediate mitigations: lower default max_new_tokens for int4 to 96, add slot_reserve=8MB, and bump batch_window_ms to 25-30ms to avoid transient mega-batches.

nina: also consider a partial spill (slowspill) to host RAM instead of full evict. config: slowspill.enabled=true partial_threshold=0.75 spill_rate=0.5. that flattens IO peaks.

jo: proposed canary patch: 
- default.max_new_tokens: 96 for orion-9b:int4
- batch_window_ms: 30
- slot_reserve: 8MB
- slowspill.enabled: true, partial_threshold: 0.75, spill_rate: 0.5
- concurrency_soft_cap: 0.6 when frag_index > 0.35
I'll run a 2h smoke with rps bursts and capture alloc_hist, frag_index timeline, evict_count, host_swap_io.

raj: perf plan: microbench 8k short chats (prompt 40 tokens) + 300 long sessions (prompt 1024). record p50/p95/p99 and cost/tokens. watch for host CPU spike with slowspill.

nina: QA guard: run a 200-prompt eval comparing generations to baseline. block canary if avg Cohen's d > 0.05 or truncation increases >1.5%. Also log per-route fallback counts.

ops-bot: deploy scheduled: canary/orion-9b-int4 -> 1731001200. Alert rules: host_swap_io > 110MB/s for 5m -> auto-rollback; slab_frag_index > 0.45 -> notify oncall.

jo: starting canary in ~10m. will post short results + logs after the smoke. ping me if you want heap-tag traces — I can enable them mid-run. :thumbsup:
